items.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: my uncle owned a nightclub and I had an opportunity to work there from time to time because he’d employ all my favorite people like Louis Armstrong and Duke Ellington

ctx.x: Phoebe, I just have this curiosity about how did you become such an unbelievable supporter and lover of jazz music?

Well I guess like anything else I just took to the music. And my uncle owned a nightclub and I had an opportunity to work there from time to time because he’d employ all my favorite people like Louis Armstrong and Duke Ellington and Ella Fitzgerald and Count Basie and so forth, so I got involved. And I became so enamored of their artistry and I became so affected by what they had to go through to succeed. Because we are living in such a racial situation that’s so terrible, yet I could recognize that they were…

Did you have education or training for some of the things that you ended up doing, being a publicist and a promoter and all those kinds of things, or did you learn on the job? © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
